target_name: Claims-based profit yield free of fixed capital
rationale: The composite is internally consistent (asset-heaviness per dollar of price enters negatively, matching the hypothesis) and SUMRANK avoids the mechanical degeneracy that a MIN of two ME-scaled legs would create, but the stated diagnosis is only half right — one of the two large archive alphas came from depreciation-to-price, not non-current-assets-to-price — and the fixed-capital leg carried a negative FMB slope, so the two channels may fight cross-sectionally.

Swapping the value leg from book-to-market to the claims-based gross-profit yield while holding the liquidity conditioner fixed is a legitimate one-variable test of whether the HML loading or the solvency screen drives the archive's only both-positive result, though it remains an incremental recombination of two already-evaluated legs and risks double-penalizing liabilities (in the denominator and again via act−lt).

Both legs scale by market equity in opposite directions — low price raises leg 1 and pushes leg 2 more negative — so MIN will be pinned to the fixed-capital leg for exactly the cheap firms the hypothesis targets, making the signal largely a rescaled rediscovery of the archive's Liquidation-backed value gap rather than a clean horse race.

Subtracting dp from the numerator of an already-evaluated archive expression is a near-cosmetic single-term tweak, and the resulting construct (post-depreciation operating profit over market equity plus liabilities) is essentially the published enterprise-multiple/profits-to-EV anomaly.

The economic question (which liabilities actually make cheapness dangerous) is real and unsettled in the archive, but the expression is gross-profits-to-enterprise-value — a standard, widely documented valuation multiple — and is only a denominator substitution on an already-evaluated signal.

The conditioner does not compute what the hypothesis describes: Δ(act−lct) includes changes in cash and short-term debt, so cash accumulation is scored as bad accruals and short-term borrowing as good, and the underlying accrual channel is the canonical Sloan anomaly rather than a novel interaction — netting che and dlc out of working capital would be the minimum fix.
